hypothesis: If perissodactyls are closer to hares and rabbits than to other ungulates, divergence-time data will show the Perissodactyla–Leporidae common ancestor is more recent than the Perissodactyla–Artiodactyla one.
pass_criterion: TimeTree gives a median divergence time for Perissodactyla–Leporidae that is younger than that for Perissodactyla–Artiodactyla, and Leporidae are closer to Perissodactyla than to Rodentia.
fail_criterion: The Perissodactyla–Artiodactyla divergence is younger than the Perissodactyla–Leporidae one, or Leporidae are closer to Rodentia than to Perissodactyla.
interpretation: 'Ungulates' is read as the sampled hoofed orders (Artiodactyla, with cetaceans nested within). 'Closer related' is read as a more recent common ancestor in a dated molecular tree. Thompson's evidence was the geometric transformation of skulls, so this tests his phylogenetic conclusion, not the geometry.

dataset.name: TimeTree – The Timescale of Life
dataset.why_it_fits: TimeTree gives pairwise divergence times between taxa, aggregated from published studies. The pairs (Perissodactyla, Leporidae), (Perissodactyla, Artiodactyla) and (Leporidae, Rodentia) are queried.
